title: How data journalism is done on TikTok: six key takeaways from watching 50 videos
content:
Short-form vertical video is quickly becoming a key format for telling all types of news stories — and data journalism is no exception.

As a data journalist, I wanted to know how these outlets use this new and evolving digital video format to create “data shorts”: short-form social media videos in a vertical, reel-style format, that analyses or reports on specific datasets or newly released data.

I analysed 50 data shorts from the TikTok accounts of five major UK news publications — the BBC, ITV News, Guardian, Times and Financial Times — to examine how these digital news outlets approach the format. I looked at the genre of story they covered, the angles they focused on, their length, and their use of animation, to help inform my guidelines.

My analysed data shorts averaged a runtime of just under 84 seconds.

The BBC ranked lowest for average video length, at just under a minute, while the Financial Times had the highest at 105 seconds.

Notably, none of the publications had an average video length over two minutes, despite TikTok allowing longer uploads up to 60 minutes.
